title: Initialize a repository
description: Turn your workspace into a Git repository. There's a single command that starts tracking a folder with Git — find it.

title: Make your first commit
description: Create a file, stage it, and record it as a commit with a message. Three separate steps — create, stage, commit.

title: Check repository status
description: Change a file that's already tracked, then check what Git thinks is different in your working directory right now.

title: Create a new branch named 'dev'
description: Branches let you work on something without touching main. Create one called 'dev'.

title: Switch to the 'dev' branch
description: Move your working directory so it's pointing at 'dev' instead of wherever you are now.

title: Merge 'dev' into 'main'
description: Bring the work on 'dev' back into 'main'. Think about which branch you need to be standing on before you run the merge.

title: Stash your changes
description: You've got uncommitted changes you're not ready to commit, but you need a clean working directory. Shelve them without losing them.

title: Tag a commit
description: Mark your current commit as a release point named `v1.0` so you can always find it later, even after history moves on.

title: Delete the 'dev' branch
description: Now that dev's work is merged, it's clutter. Remove the branch (not the commits — those are safe in main).

title: Rebase a branch
description: Create a branch called `feature` and commit at least one change on it. Then replay those commits on top of main's current tip instead of merging — the result should be a straight line of history, no merge commit.

title: Cherry-pick a commit
description: You want just ONE commit from `feature`, not the whole branch, applied to `main`. Find its commit hash and bring only that one across.

title: Clone from the practice remote
description: There's a bare Git repo waiting for you on the git-server at `git://git-server/<your-reg-no>/practice.git`. Get a working copy of it onto your machine.

title: Push to the remote
description: Commit a change on `main` in your cloned copy, then send that commit up to the remote so it's reflected there too.

title: Pull from the remote
description: The remote has moved ahead of your local copy (fetch it and see). Bring your local `main` up to date with the remote in one step.

title: Resolve a merge conflict
description: Set up two branches that each change the same line of the same file differently. Merge one into the other, deal with the conflict Git can't resolve on its own, and finish the merge.
